close_reason: Already fixed in commit d848962: message_id sanitization now includes '\r' and '\n' in the replace chain at inbound.rs:107
description: In inbound.rs note_to_article, the message_id is constructed from note_id via sanitization (replacing some chars) but the result is embedded directly into the article bytes without a CRLF strip: article.push_str(&format!("Message-ID: {message_id}\r\n")). The sanitized value replaces / and some chars but does NOT strip \r or \n from the sanitized result. An adversarially crafted note id that survives the replace chain containing encoded CRLF sequences (%0d%0a for example, which are not replaced) could inject headers. The safe_irt variable for In-Reply-To IS stripped of CR/LF, but message_id is not.
title: inbound note_to_article: message_id not sanitised before embedding in header
